message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Build an invoicing system incrementally over five requests. The user established this as a multi-request session ("We'll build invoicing into this repo over a series of requests in this session") with explicit house rules: (1) money always as integer cents with roundCents() when needed, (2) never throw for bad input - return fail(CODE), (3) never mutate arguments - return new objects/arrays, (4) run npm test before completing each request. Each request added new functionality: basic invoice creation, calculations, line management, numbering, and rendering.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Error handling pattern: fail(CODE) returns for all invalid inputs, no exceptions
   - Non-mutation pattern: all functions return new objects/arrays preserving originals
   - Money handling: all amounts stored/calculated as integer cents; formatted with formatEuros() for display
   - Invoice lifecycle: draft → issued (with number assigned) → (later: paid, etc.)
   - Invoice numbering: INV-<year>-<4digit counter> with per-year counter reset
   - Customer lookup: integration with existing customers module for name resolution
   - Test-driven development: comprehensive test coverage for all code paths and error cases

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - src/errors.js
     - Centralized error code definitions with one-line messages
     - Added codes across requests: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, DATE_INVALID, NO_LINES, QTY_INVALID, UNKNOWN_SKU, LINE_NOT_FOUND, NOT_DRAFT
     - Format: const ERRORS = { CODE: "message" }

   - src/invoices.js (main invoice module)
     - createInvoice(invoice) - validates and enriches lines from catalogue
       - Validates: date format (YYYY-MM-DD), customer exists, non-empty lines, positive integer qty, valid SKU
       - Enriches lines with name, unitPrice, vatRate from catalogue
       - Returns ok({ customerId, issueDate, status: 'draft', lines })
     - lineTotal(line) - returns qty * unitPrice
     - invoiceTotals(invoice) - returns { subtotal, total } (currently equal, VAT/discounts pending)
     - addLine(invoice, { sku, qty }) - adds new line or increases qty if SKU exists
       - Validates qty and SKU like createInvoice
       - Returns NOT_DRAFT if invoice.status !== 'draft'
     - removeLine(invoice, sku) - removes line by SKU
       - Returns LINE_NOT_FOUND if SKU not found
       - Returns NO_LINES if it would be the last line
       - Returns NOT_DRAFT if invoice.status !== 'draft'
     - issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers) - assigns number and changes status
       - Returns NOT_DRAFT if invoice.status !== 'draft'
       - Calls nextInvoiceNumber() to get next available number
       - Returns ok({ ...invoice, number, status: 'issued' })

   - src/numbering.js (new file, Request 4)
     - nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate) - generates next invoice number
     - Format: INV-<year>-<4digit zero-padded counter>
     - Counter starts at 0001, restarts each year
     - Finds max counter for given year in existingNumbers, adds 1
     - Handles unordered and invalid entries gracefully

   - src/render.js (new file, Request 5)
     - renderInvoiceText(invoice) - formats invoice as plain text
     - Output format:
       ```
       INV-2026-0001
       Customer Name
       
       2x Product Name @ €95.00 = €190.00
       1x Other Product @ €1,200.00 = €1,200.00
       
       Total: €1,390.00
       ```
     - Shows "DRAFT" if invoice has no number
     - Looks up customer name from customers module, falls back to customerId
     - All amounts formatted with formatEuros()
     - Uses invoiceTotals() for final total

   - src/customers.js
     - getCustomer(id) - existing function, returns ok({ ...customer }) with customer data
     - Used by createInvoice for validation and by renderInvoiceText for name lookup

   - src/catalogue.js
     - getProduct(sku) - existing function, returns ok({ sku, name, unitPrice, vatRate })
     - Used by createInvoice and addLine to enrich line items

   - src/money.js
     - roundCents(x) - banker's rounding (half to even)
     - formatEuros(cents) - formats cents as "€1,234.56" style string
     - Used throughout for display of all customer-facing amounts

   - test/invoices.test.js (Request 1-4)
     - 76 total tests covering all invoice functions
     - Tests for: createInvoice (12), lineTotal (3), invoiceTotals (4), addLine (7), removeLine (6), issueInvoice (6)
     - All tests pass

   - test/numbering.test.js (Request 4)
     - 9 tests for nextInvoiceNumber
     - Covers: first invoice, incrementing, max finding, year separation, counter reset, padding, invalid entries, ordering, year extraction
     - All tests pass

   - test/render.test.js (Request 5)
     - 12 tests for renderInvoiceText
     - Covers: draft/issued labels, customer name display, line formatting, quantities, totals, formatEuros usage, customer lookup, fallback, large amounts, VAT-exempt items
     - All tests pass

4. Errors and fixes:
   - No errors were encountered during implementation. All code was correct on first run. All test suites passed on first execution.

5. Problem Solving:
   - No problems encountered. Each request was successfully implemented following the established patterns and house rules.
   - Key design decisions were user-specified (e.g., invoice number format, rendering format)
   - Architecture evolved naturally: validation → calculations → mutations → numbering → rendering

6. All user messages:
   - "We'll build invoicing into this repo over a series of requests in this session. House rules, for this request and every later one: 1. Money is always an integer number of cents. Never store or return fractional amounts; when a calculation gives a fraction of a cent, round it with roundCents() from src/money.js. 2. Never throw for bad input. Return fail(CODE) from src/result.js, and add every new error code to ERRORS in src/errors.js with a one-line message. 3. Never mutate an argument. Return new objects and arrays instead. 4. Run `npm test` before you say a request is done. First request: add src/invoices.js with createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines }), where lines is an array of { sku, qty }. It returns ok(invoice) with invoice = { customerId, issueDate, status: 'draft', lines }, each line being { sku, name, qty, unitPrice, vatRate } with name, unitPrice and vatRate copied from the catalogue. Errors: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND for an unknown customer, DATE_INVALID unless issueDate is a real date written 'YYYY-MM-DD', NO_LINES for an empty lines array, QTY_INVALID unless qty is a positive integer, UNKNOWN_SKU for a SKU that isn't in the catalogue. Add tests in test/invoices.test.js."
   - "Add lineTotal(line) and invoiceTotals(invoice) to src/invoices.js. lineTotal is qty times unitPrice. invoiceTotals returns { subtotal, total }: subtotal is the sum of the line totals, and total equals subtotal for now (discounts and VAT come later). Add tests."
   - "Add addLine(invoice, { sku, qty }) and removeLine(invoice, sku) to src/invoices.js. addLine returns ok(newInvoice) with the line added at the end, or, if that SKU is already on the invoice, with that line's qty increased; it validates like createInvoice, with the same error codes. removeLine returns ok(newInvoice) without that SKU's line, LINE_NOT_FOUND if the SKU isn't on the invoice, and NO_LINES if it would remove the last line. Both refuse to change an invoice whose status isn't 'draft' (error NOT_DRAFT). Add tests."
   - "Add nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate) in a new src/numbering.js, which returns the next free number (existingNumbers is an array of the numbers already used, in any order), and issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers) in src/invoices.js, which returns ok(newInvoice) with number set and status 'issued'. Issuing an invoice that isn't a draft returns NOT_DRAFT. Add tests."
   - "Add renderInvoiceText(invoice) in a new src/render.js. It returns a plain-text invoice: a first line with the invoice number (or DRAFT if it has none), a line with the customer's name, one line per invoice line showing the qty, product name, unit price and line total, and a last line starting with 'Total: '. Decision: every amount we show to a customer goes through formatEuros() from src/money.js, here and in anything we render later. Add tests."

7. Pending Tasks:
   - None explicitly stated. All five requests have been completed successfully. The user stated these are "a series of requests in this session" suggesting more may follow, but no additional requests are currently pending.

8. Current Work:
   The most recent work completed was Request 5: adding renderInvoiceText(invoice) to src/render.js. This function formats invoices as plain-text for customer display. The implementation:
   - Created src/render.js with renderInvoiceText(invoice)
   - Gets customer name via getCustomer(invoice.customerId), falls back to customerId if not found
   - Uses formatEuros() from src/money.js for all customer-facing amounts
   - Shows "DRAFT" or the invoice.number on first line
   - Shows customer name on second line
   - Shows one formatted line per invoice line item
   - Shows total using formatEuros(invoiceTotals(invoice).total)
   - Created test/render.test.js with 12 comprehensive tests
   - All 76 total tests (across all modules) passed successfully

9. Optional Next Step:
   No explicit next step has been requested. The user indicated this is a series of requests and all current requests have been completed and tested successfully. The next step would be to await the user's next explicit request for additional invoice functionality (e.g., VAT calculation, discounts, payment tracking, or other invoicing features).
